turns.content: Hi. I've got Section 4 of the Master Services Agreement open — specifically 4.2 on notice periods and 4.3 on rollover terms. Clara sent her written rollover notice on March 14, and the quarterly billing reconciliation closes March 31. Excluding weekends, that gives 12 business days. Section 4.2 requires at least 10 business days' notice. So my reading is she cleared the minimum. Just want to confirm that's consistent with the clause language. Does that sound right?

**On the numbers you’ve given, yes:** 12 business days exceeds the “at least 10 business days” minimum.

But I’d need to see **Sections 4.2 and 4.3** to confirm that’s consistent with the clause language—particularly whether:
- March 31’s reconciliation close is the deadline the notice period runs against;
- notice is effective when **sent or received**; and
- “business days” excludes holidays as well as weekends.

If those points line up with your assumptions, Clara cleared the minimum. Paste the two clauses and I can check the wording directly.

Right — sent or received isn't spelled out in 4.2, but Clara's email header shows it was transmitted before 5pm on the 14th, so I'm treating it as effective that day. Holidays: none fell in that window, so I think the 12 still holds. Does that match your read of what the clause would assume, or does 4.2 say something about effective date I'm missing?

The email header supports **transmission on March 14**, but it doesn’t by itself establish that the contract treats notice as effective that day.

**I haven’t seen Section 4.2**, so I can’t tell whether there’s effective-date language you’re missing. If it’s silent, check the MSA’s general **Notices** provision for permitted delivery methods, deemed receipt, and any time-of-day cutoff. Sending before 5 p.m. matters only if the applicable notice rules make it relevant.

Your conclusion remains conditional: **if the notice was effective March 14, March 31 is the relevant deadline, and the count is 12 business days under the agreement, she met the 10-day minimum.** Paste 4.2, 4.3, and any general Notices provision so I can check the actual wording.

Okay, that makes sense. So, on "unused retainer hours" under 4.2 — our retainer pools design and strategy hours together into a blended monthly total, not separated. The clause doesn't specify whether the rollover cap applies per service line or to the whole pool. My reading is it applies to the total pool. Does the text seem to support that, or is it ambiguous enough I should flag it?

**Applying the cap to the total pool is a plausible reading based on your description—but I can’t confirm the text supports it without seeing it.**

If the agreement defines the retainer as one blended monthly allocation of design and strategy hours, and 4.2 refers simply to “unused retainer hours,” that would favor a **single cap on the combined pool**. Silence about service lines doesn’t, by itself, establish separate caps.

I’d flag it for clarification if another provision or the statement of work separates those allocations, or if the two interpretations would materially change the rollover amount. A neutral flag could be:

> “Our reading is that the rollover cap applies once to the combined design-and-strategy retainer pool, rather than separately to each service line. Please confirm.”

Paste 4.2–4.3 and the retainer definition or allocation language, and I can assess whether that reading is supported or the wording leaves a meaningful ambiguity.

Right — that's helpful. So rollover hours used in Q2, would they stay capped at the 20-hour maximum in 4.2, or does that cap reset each quarter? Also, Section 4.4 says out-of-scope ad-hoc hours don't roll over — that seems clear, but just checking if I'm reading it right.

**The 20-hour cap’s treatment in Q2 isn’t established by what you’ve shared.** I haven’t seen the clauses, and a “20-hour maximum” could mean:
- **A carryover limit:** no more than 20 hours can transfer into each eligible period.
- **A balance limit:** the accumulated rollover balance can never exceed 20 hours.

Those have different effects. Neither necessarily limits how many rollover hours can be *used* during Q2, and a quarterly billing reconciliation doesn’t by itself mean the cap resets quarterly. We’d need 4.2–4.3’s wording on the rollover period, accumulation, and expiration.

**On 4.4: yes, if it says out-of-scope ad-hoc hours don’t roll over, your reading matches that description.** Those hours would be excluded from rollover, rather than included subject to the 20-hour cap.

Please paste 4.2–4.4 so I can distinguish what the agreement actually says from these possible interpretations.

Wait — 4.2 says "rollover hours used in the subsequent quarter shall be subject to the maximum set forth herein." That's the exact language. So it reads like the 20-hour cap applies to usage in Q2, not just carryover. Does "subject to the maximum" mean each quarter's usage is capped, or just that the rollover itself can't exceed 20?

**That sentence more directly supports a cap on usage in Q2**, rather than solely a cap on hours carried into Q2. The key wording is **“rollover hours used in the subsequent quarter”**—those hours are expressly made subject to the maximum.

If “the maximum set forth herein” refers to the 20-hour limit, the natural reading is that **no more than 20 rollover hours may be used in the subsequent quarter**. That qualifies my earlier distinction: the quoted sentence does connect the cap to usage.

It does **not, by itself, establish a fresh allowance or reset each quarter**. Nor does it resolve whether unused rollover hours expire, can carry forward again, or are also subject to a balance cap. Those questions depend on the surrounding language.

So: **Q2 usage capped at 20 is the stronger reading of this sentence; an automatic quarterly reset is not established.** The sentence that originally sets the maximum, together with 4.3, would help resolve the rest.
